bash.notes: Buildroot package provider; stages .bashrc when bash dotfiles are enabled.

zsh.notes: May increase payload size and may need modules or terminfo depending on build options.

tmux.notes: Needs /dev/pts, usable ptys, and terminal capability data.

strace.notes: Requires ptrace support and architecture-specific syscall decoding.

build_failures.reason: Buildroot GDB 15.x BFD fails to link for mipsel/mips musl targets; gdbserver is pre-excluded in best-effort mode

known_provider_issues.message: Buildroot GDB/BFD is known to fail for mipsel/mips+musl/static builds. The gdbserver Buildroot package will be pre-excluded in best-effort mode.
known_provider_issues.suggested_action: Use provider=local-dropin with local/tools/<target>/bin/gdbserver, provider=user with a pre-built static binary, or provider=overlay with the binary under your overlay root/target/bin/.

gdbserver.notes: Requires ptrace and enough target memory for debug sessions. On mipsel/mips+musl the full GDB BFD library fails to build; use STRICT_HEAVY_TOOLS=1 to treat this as a fatal error. Use BB_GDBSERVER_PROVIDER=local-dropin, user, or overlay to supply a pre-built binary.

dropbear.notes: Server mode needs writable storage for host keys and usable ptys for interactive sessions.

curl.notes: TLS-enabled builds can increase payload size and may need CA data.

socat.notes: Buildroot package provider; useful for relays, serial devices, and quick socket tests.

tcpdump.notes: Requires packet capture permissions and usable network interfaces on target.

mtr.notes: May require raw socket privileges for full diagnostics.

ethtool.notes: Requires kernel driver support for device-specific details.

iw.notes: Requires cfg80211/nl80211 support and wireless hardware.

minicom.notes: Needs a usable serial device and terminal settings.

mosh-client.notes: Client-only staging from Buildroot mosh package; needs UDP connectivity to server.

ripgrep.notes: Buildroot Rust package; may increase host build requirements and build time.

htop.notes: Interactive ncurses UI; needs terminal support.

screen.notes: Needs ptys and terminal capability data.

ltrace.notes: Requires ptrace support and architecture-specific ltrace support.

xxd.notes: Provided by the BusyBox applet set when enabled.

usbutils.notes: Stages lsusb; output depends on usbfs/sysfs availability.

pciutils.notes: Stages lspci; many embedded targets do not expose PCI hardware.

gdb.static_constraints: Target-side full gdb is heavy and may require Python/termcap support; prefer target gdbserver with operator-side gdb.
gdb.notes: Do not include in default presets. Use local drop-in or overlay only when target-side gdb is explicitly validated.

gef-pwndbg.static_constraints: Requires operator-side gdb with Python plugin support.
gef-pwndbg.notes: Keep GEF/pwndbg-style helpers on the operator workstation unless a target-side Python gdb stack is explicitly selected.

nmap.notes: Useful for local network diagnostics; not included in default presets.

nmap-ncat.static_constraints: Uses the Buildroot nmap package ncat suboption.
nmap-ncat.notes: Complements BusyBox nc/netcat when richer relay features are needed.

psmisc.static_constraints: Buildroot package provides pstree/fuser/killall variants depending on configuration.
psmisc.notes: Partly overlaps BusyBox process applets; select only when pstree/fuser behavior is needed.

openssl.static_constraints: Static builds may be large; dynamic builds may need bundled shared libraries.
openssl.notes: Useful as an operator diagnostic and TLS helper, but not required for builtin TLS.

fd.static_constraints: Rust package; static availability depends on active Buildroot/toolchain support.
fd.notes: Nice-to-have search helper; BusyBox find remains the default baseline.

zoxide.static_constraints: Rust package; needs shell integration files to be useful interactively.
zoxide.notes: Shell convenience tool, not selected by default.

radare2.static_constraints: No Buildroot mapping in the checked tree.
radare2.notes: Reverse-engineering suites are too large and variable for default payload generation.

rizin.static_constraints: No Buildroot mapping in the checked tree.
rizin.notes: Requires a target-compatible drop-in or overlay binary until a target tuple has a validated package path.

gcore.static_constraints: Usually part of a full gdb stack and requires ptrace/core dump policy support.
gcore.notes: Prefer gdbserver and operator-side gdb for capture workflows.

tshark.static_constraints: Wireshark/tshark is too heavy for default static payloads in this tree.
tshark.notes: Use tcpdump by default; stage tshark only as a validated provider binary.

mtd-utils.static_constraints: Requires Linux MTD device support and root permissions for most operations.
mtd-utils.notes: Flash tools can irreversibly alter devices; keep behind explicit dangerous storage/flash selection.

ubi-utils.static_constraints: Requires UBI kernel support and root permissions for most operations.
ubi-utils.notes: Do not include in default/full-debug presets.

i2c-tools.notes: Bus probing may affect hardware; select explicitly.

mmc-utils.static_constraints: Requires MMC block device access; dangerous commands are not enabled by default.
mmc-utils.notes: Keep destructive MMC commands out unless explicitly needed.

e2fsprogs.static_constraints: Static builds may be larger; some tools need block device write access.
e2fsprogs.notes: Includes filesystem inspection and repair tools such as debugfs/tune2fs/e2fsck depending on package options.

parted.static_constraints: Requires block device access and libparted dependencies.
parted.notes: Partition editors are explicitly dangerous and should never be default-selected.

doom.classification: optional runtime with user-provided WAD data
doom.expected_payload_size: small engine plus user-staged WAD data
doom.static_constraints: Buildroot provider builds doom-ascii statically; user/provider binaries must match the target architecture and libc.
doom.notes: Classic Doom-compatible terminal runtime. Target builds compile doom-ascii statically through Buildroot and stage only the user-provided WAD from BB_DOOM_WAD_PATH; BusierBox does not download game data.
